SPAR F26 · Indonesia lane · S5 hiring signal · preliminary scrape test

Individual job postings, not just aggregates — Karirhub, Jan 2024 – Oct 2026, finance & BPO

First successful pass on the team's row format (timestamp · location · content · AI-skill flag · public/private). 2618 postings recovered for the window Jan 2024 – 20 Oct 2026 (the live portal covers only the newest year; older rows are Web Archive captures), of which 512 fall in the finance/BPO scope. Every row is traceable to a public URL. This is a sample, not a census.

Headline: the block that stopped the Hermes attempt was the Algolia search API — we routed around it by harvesting detail-page URLs and reading server-rendered posting pages. Algolia is still unreachable here; Kalibrr and bank-portal APIs still refuse us.

What this proves. A timestamped, location-tagged, content-bearing panel of Indonesian finance-sector vacancies is obtainable from public data without an access request. The live portal is dense only for the newest listings; the Web Archive backfill now adds Feb 2024 – Oct 2025, but only the pages the archive happened to crawl, so monthly volumes are uneven. A genuine monthly series needs the same crawl repeated from now on. The AI-skill question is answerable in principle (1 explicit hits, 22 data-skill hits, 156 "digital-basic" postings), but the base rate is low enough that keyword flags alone will not carry Dani's and Akbar's classification — that needs the deferred LLM/human pass on the stored content.

The detailed data — 2618 rows in the requested format

Sortable and filterable. AI-skill required? is the keyword flag; domain is PUBLIC for every row (source URLs included). Download: the Google Sheet (the CSV ships as data/id-postings/postings-<year>.csv, one file per year).

# posted ↕ location content — title / employer / snippet / skills / Persyaratan Khusus AI-skill? verified? source links domain

How real is each row? See the “verified?” column and the sources section above. Checked 2026-11-04 with build/verify_postings.py, which re-fetches source URLs. Live (281) — verified: all returned 200 and matched the portal's own title, posting date, deadline, employer and location. Archive (2337) — weaker: 177 were re-fetched (the first 50 in full, plus a random sample of 100 of the Feb 2024 – Oct 2025 backfill) and all matched on title, location and employer; the other 2160 were parsed once from the capture and not independently re-checked. Archive dates are derived from the relative label on the captured page ("3 days ago"); 1559 of the backfill rows carry only a month-level label ("3 months ago"), so their date can be off by about ±15 days. 5 archive rows have no employer name, 83 have no skills list, and the finance / not-finance label on every archive row is a keyword guess on title and employer.

Persyaratan Khusus (the portal's "special requirements" section) is captured for 2457 of 2618 rows — 196 of 281 live, 2261 of 2337 archive. Open the section under each row's snippet; the CSV column requirements carries the full text. A row without it means the portal shows no such section for that posting, not a failed fetch.

The CSV also carries ai_evidence / data_evidence — the exact matched term behind each flag, so any row can be audited.

Timestamps: live rows use the platform's own publishedAt (exact). Archive rows are derived from the relative label on the captured page ("2 days ago") and are marked as such in the CSV's posted_basis.

AI-skill signal — the team's question, first cut

Two independent flags per posting. AI-skill is decided by the posting's own Persyaratan Khusus, as the team asked: Yes only when that section names an AI skill or tool (kecerdasan buatan, machine learning, ChatGPT, prompt engineering, computer vision, an AI tool, …). Data-skill covers data analysis, SQL, Python, BI; digital-basic is ordinary literacy only (Excel, Office, "komputer").

Counts: 3 rows are Yes out of 2618. A further 5 mention AI only in the ad description (not as a stated requirement) — they stay No and are recorded as context in ai_evidence. 161 rows have no Persyaratan Khusus section at all, so for those the flag rests on the description alone and is weaker.

How the AI flag is decided now — and what went wrong before

The flag used to come from a loose keyword pass over title, description and skills. That pass was wrong in both directions, and this build replaces it:

  • False positives: keras fired on the everyday Indonesian word pekerja keras ("diligent worker") — 66 rows; genai fired inside mengenai ("regarding"); ai tools fired inside Menguasai tools; llm fired inside fulfillment; and "AI" in a design ad is usually Adobe Illustrator, not artificial intelligence.
  • False negatives: the flag never looked at Persyaratan Khusus, the section where a posting actually states the skills it wants.

Now: the posting's Persyaratan Khusus decides, with word boundaries everywhere, an explicit list of AI terms and named tools, and Adobe-Illustrator disambiguation. Result: 3 rows are Yes — every one of them quoting the requirement that matched, visible in the tooltip and in ai_evidence, so each can be checked by hand. 5 more mention AI only in the description and are deliberately not counted. Automation-only wording (RPA, "otomasi", "big data", "predictive") is not counted as AI either.

Interpretation: in this sample AI requirements are near-absent from advertised BPO and banking postings. That is a finding about advertised entry-level demand — Indonesian bank/BPO ads for frontline and collections roles rarely list tooling. It does not show that AI skills are not used on the job. Widen the sample before drawing an S5 conclusion.

Where the postings come from — and how far each is verified

Every row links to the page it was read from. Source of the postings: employers publish them on Karirhub, the Ministry of Manpower's (Kemnaker) job portal; we read the public detail page. Archive rows are the same page as saved by the Internet Archive (Wayback Machine), so they carry two links: the capture and the original posting.

Unverified = the source did not load or a field did not match (0 rows). Not re-checked = parsed from the source once, never independently re-fetched (2160 rows). Blocked ≠ absent: JobStreet, Indeed, LinkedIn, Kalibrr and the banks all hold finance postings. They are simply gated, and the gate is the finding for the public/private split.

Was this done ethically?

Marks against the checklist the team agreed: robots/ToS, personal data, access gating, re-publication, and honesty about coverage.

PASSrobots.txt respected
karirhub.kemnaker.go.id/robots.txt is User-agent: * → Allow: / with only admin/dashboard/api/login disallowed. We fetched only public /lowongan-dalam-negeri/lowongan/… pages and never touched the disallowed paths.
PASSNo personal data
No applicant names, CVs, e-mail addresses, phone numbers or recruiter contacts were collected. Rows hold company names only, as published in the public advertisement — consistent with data/PERSONAL-DATA-STOP.md.
PASSIdentified crawler + rate limit
Requests carried User-Agent: SPAR-F26-research/0.1 (academic feasibility test) and slept ~0.35 s between pages (~1.5k pages, single-threaded pool of 4). No parallel hammering, no retries against 4xx.
CAVEATNo anti-bot circumvention
We did not spoof tokens, rotate proxies or solve challenges. Where a platform refused us (Kalibrr KJS API 400/404, BCA candidate API 403, JobStreet/Indeed 403) we recorded the refusal and stopped — that is why those arms are absent, not because the data does not exist.
PASSPublic domain only
Every row is PUBLIC: a government portal page (live arm) or its public Internet Archive capture (archive arm). No logins, no paid feeds, no access requests were used.
CAVEATMinimal re-publication
Ad text is truncated to 240 characters and skills/attributes are kept as short fields, so the repo does not become a wholesale mirror of the platform. Full text stays in local scratch only.
CAVEATCoverage-bias caveat stated
The count of rows here is not the number of vacancies that existed. Live listings only survive while open, so the panel is recency-skewed; archive captures are uneven. Every chart below is labelled as a sample, not a census.
CAVEATAdvertised demand ≠ hires
Postings measure advertised labour demand. They do not establish hiring rates, filled positions or employment — the distinction the team flagged for the IMF-inspired scenario work.
Short answer: yes — this slice is public-domain, robots-permitted, rate-limited, contains no personal data, and did not bypass any access control. The two caveats are deliberate: we truncated ad text rather than mirroring the platform, and we refuse to present the sample size as a vacancy count.

What to refine next (and what would change the answer)

Cheap wins

  • Re-run the live crawl monthly; the same script keeps the panel current and turns the sample into a series.
  • Widen keyword harvesting (teller, collection, underwriting, fintech, paylater) — the current 281 is one keyword sweep, not a full month.
  • Archive rows before 20 Oct 2025 are now included (Jan 2024 – Oct 2025). The gap that remains is Nov 2025 – Jul 2026, where we have only a sample.
  • Store full descriptions locally, classify with an LLM pass, ship only the flags — Akbar's "whichever is more convenient".

What still blocks a real S5 panel

  • No historical depth on the live portal: closed postings disappear, so pre-Aug-2026 is archive-only.
  • Kalibrr / bank portals hold better-structured data but are gated — needs permission, not cleverness.
  • Duplicate detection across employer aliases (PT X vs X) is unsolved; the 32 Kasih Anugrah rows are one employer, many city-level postings.
  • Postings ≠ hires. For a hiring-rate signal we need a second data source (employment statistics, or job-board fill indicators).
